2.text: Chukchee on the Arctic shore, 1600, which should be increased to 2000,

3.text: because I omitted in my enumeration some of the minor settlements the names
3.note: Machine text appended a trailing comma after 'names'; the print has none at the line-wrap (sheet zoom, lines 2-9).

4.text: of which I obtained, but which I was unable to identify with villages mentioned

5.text: by Lieut. Nordquist. Lieut. Nordquist arrives at the same number of inhabitants,

6.text: but the number of houses in his list are more than 400, as compared with

7.text: 266 enumerated by me. His estimate is based, according to his own statement,

8.text: on the assumption of only five persons to a house, whereas my figure is six
8.note: A small curved mark sits below-left of the 's' in 'six' (4x zoom, 8@88). 'six' is plain English with no licensed sub-s mark in the inventory, and the mark does not sit under the letter cleanly the way a genuine diacritic would - read as a stray ink speck/smudge, per keying_spec.md §5.9 ('key the letter as printed... let a human rule'). Keyed 'six' plain; flagging for adjudication rather than proposing an uncatalogued codepoint.

9.text: and a half. With an equal average of inmates to a house, his census of the

10.text: population on the Arctic shores would exceed mine by 600. It seems probable,

11.text: therefore, as Mr. Gondatti asserts, that the maritime population has diminished

12.text: of late years. His assumption, however, that the Arctic shore is more thickly

13.text: populated than the Pacific, seems to me unfounded.

14.text: The total number of the Chukchee amounts to 12,000, rather more than

15.text: less, of which three fourths are reindeer-breeders, and only one fourth maritime.

16.text: The decrease in the maritime population may be partly accounted for by the

17.text: fact that each year many families turn from maritime pursuits to reindeer-

19.text: Several villages have nearly or altogether disappeared, because all the

20.text: inhabitants have gone inland and have turned reindeer-breeders. These are,

21.text: on the Arctic coast, besides those of Kuluˊči Bay, mentioned above, the
21.resolved: Kuluˊči: Kulu + ˊ (U+02CA stress, postposed to u) + či (c + U+030C caron)
21.note: Raised mark after 'Kulu' read as stress U+02CA (keying_spec.md §4: a raised mark defaults to stress, never apostrophe). Confirmed at 4x (21@45).

22.text: villages Reᵋn, Ot-ᴇnmɪtaˊhɪn, Paloˊnnan; on the Pacific coast, Kuˊkun, Čeˊnlin,
22.resolved: Reᵋn: R + e + ᵋ (U+1D4B laryngeal superscript, glottalization) + n. Ot-ᴇnmɪtaˊhɪn: ᴇ = U+1D07 small-cap E; ɪ = U+026A small-cap dotless I (x2); ˊ = U+02CA stress, postposed to 'a'. Paloˊnnan: ˊ = U+02CA, postposed to 'o'. Kuˊkun: ˊ = U+02CA, postposed to first 'u'. Čeˊnlin: Č = C+U+030C; ˊ = U+02CA, postposed to 'e'.
22.note: The superscript after 'Re' was read at 4x (22@12) as a closed loop with a tail, not a straight tick - matches the laryngeal ᵋ (U+1D4B) rather than 'g', per the standing lesson that this mark is the one most often misread as an uncatalogued superscript g (agent memory: the-two-superscript-marks). All raised comma-shaped marks elsewhere on the line read as stress U+02CA per §4's default. Small-cap ᴇ/ɪ confirmed against the body-text capital 'O' of 'Ot' on the same word (clearly smaller) at 4x (22@8-30).

23.resolved: Wuˊkwên: ˊ = U+02CA postposed to first 'u'; ê = e + U+0302 circumflex. ᴇˊnmɪlɪn: ᴇ = U+1D07 small-cap E; ˊ = U+02CA postposed to ᴇ; ɪ = U+026A (x2).
